title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 11
paragraphs: For the moment, then, she kept silent and gave no sign. But as soon as day had dawned, she made ready those of her servants whom she knew to be most devoted to her, and sent for Gyges. He, not supposing that she knew anything of what had happened, came at her summons, for he had always been accustomed to come whenever the queen called for him. When Gyges had arrived, she said to him, “Two paths now lie open before you, Gyges, and I leave you the choice. Either kill Candaules and possess me and the kingdom of Lydia, or die here on the spot yourself, so that you shall not in future, by obeying Candaules in everything, see what you should not. One of you must die — either the man who devised this scheme, or you, who looked on me naked and did what is not permitted.” For a moment Gyges stood astonished at her words, and then began to beg her not to force such a choice on him. But when he could not move her and saw that he really had no choice but to kill his master or be killed himself, he chose to live, and asked her this: “Since you are forcing me to kill my master against my will, tell me how we are to lay hands on him.” She answered, “The attack will be made from the very same place where he displayed me naked, and we will strike him while he sleeps.”
